### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: uniform widths from the global grid; face areas are products of two widths, the volume the product of
three, the centre the midpoint. **Switch**: YAML `geometry.type: cartesian`. **Default**: this is the default type.
**Requires**: nothing. **Order**: exact. **Defining equation**: @eq-ch03-cartesian-metric.
:::

On a Cartesian grid every metric quantity is a product of cell widths, and the widths are the global $\Delta x_a$ of
@sec-ch03-globalgrid, so a cell's metric does not depend on which block holds it. The cell centre is the midpoint of
its faces, which is also the volume centroid, and the non-orthogonality cosine that the cubed sphere needs
(@sec-ch03-gnomonic) is identically zero. The finite-volume operator is the plain flux divergence; there are no
geometric source terms. The type is the default when `geometry.type` is absent.

### Derivation

For a cell $[x_{1,i-1/2}, x_{1,i+1/2}]\times[x_{2,j-1/2}, x_{2,j+1/2}]\times[x_{3,k-1/2}, x_{3,k+1/2}]$ with widths
$\Delta x_1, \Delta x_2, \Delta x_3$ the measures are the integrals of $\mathrm{d}x_2\,\mathrm{d}x_3$,
$\mathrm{d}x_1\,\mathrm{d}x_3$, $\mathrm{d}x_1\,\mathrm{d}x_2$ and $\mathrm{d}V$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{i\pm1/2} &= \Delta x_2\,\Delta x_3, \\
A_{j\pm1/2} &= \Delta x_1\,\Delta x_3, \\
A_{k\pm1/2} &= \Delta x_1\,\Delta x_2, \\
V_i &= \Delta x_1\,\Delta x_2\,\Delta x_3.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-cartesian-metric}

The face areas of @eq-ch03-cartesian-metric are `face_area1` to `face_area3` and the volume is `cell_volume`
([`coordinate.cpp:425-440`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L425-L440)). The centroid of a uniform weight over an interval is its midpoint,
$x_{1,i} = \tfrac12(x_{1,i-1/2}+x_{1,i+1/2})$, computed in `reset` for `x1v` ([`cartesian.cpp:22-28`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/cartesian.cpp#L22-L28)).
Integrating the conservation law $\partial_t q + \nabla\cdot\mathbf F = 0$ over the cell and dividing by $V_i$ gives
the update of the cell average by the face-area-weighted flux difference over the volume, with no further term,
because the basis vectors are constant. Every quantity here is exact; the executable check is the product test of
the Tests layer.

### Numerical method

Widths `dx1f`, `dx2f`, `dx3f` are cell quantities, one per cell including ghosts; `x1v` holds the midpoints; `dx1v`
(the centre spacing) equals the width. All are built once in `reset` from the global width. The divergence takes the
face fluxes $\mathbf F_a$ (face averages, from the Riemann solver), multiplies them by the face areas, differences
them across each interior cell and divides by $V_i$; ghost cells receive no divergence. @fig-ch03-cartesian-cell
draws one cell with its three face areas.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-cartesian-cell
#| fig-cap: "One Cartesian cell with its widths and the three face areas $\\Delta x_2\\Delta x_3$, $\\Delta x_1\\Delta x_3$ and $\\Delta x_1\\Delta x_2$; the centre is the midpoint."
#| fig-alt: "A box with its three widths labelled and one face of each orientation shaded."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.fig_cartesian_cell import make_fig
make_fig()
```

A mesh generator (`reset_coordinates`) may move the faces; the Cartesian override then recomputes widths, midpoints
and centre spacings from the moved faces, so the grid is no longer uniform and @eq-ch03-cartesian-metric uses the
local widths ([`cartesian.cpp:50-60`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/cartesian.cpp#L50-L60) for the $x_1$ part).

|---|---|---|---|
| widths, centres, zero cosine | [`cartesian.cpp:8-48`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/cartesian.cpp#L8-L48) | `reset` | `type: cartesian` |
| face areas and volume | [`coordinate.cpp:425-440`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L425-L440) | `cell_volume` | none |
| flux divergence | [`coordinate.cpp:509-553`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L509-L553) | `divergence` | none |
| stage operator (no source) | [`coordinate.cpp:585-591`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L585-L591) | `forward` | none |
| type selection | [`coordinate.cpp:593-610`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L593-L610) | `create` | `geometry.type` |

: Code map of the Cartesian metric. {#tbl-ch03-cartesian-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cartesian-code):

1. `create` builds a `Cartesian` module when `type` is `cartesian`; an unknown type stops setup with "Unknown
   coordinate type" ([`coordinate.cpp:593-610`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L593-L610)).
2. `reset` sets the three cosine buffers to zero and the widths, midpoints and centre spacings from the global width
   ([`cartesian.cpp:8-48`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/cartesian.cpp#L8-L48)).
3. In each stage, `forward` returns the `divergence` of the three fluxes and ignores the face pressure
   ([`coordinate.cpp:585-591`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L585-L591)); `divergence` forms the area-weighted differences over the interior cells
   and divides by `cell_volume` ([`coordinate.cpp:509-553`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L509-L553)).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate` | the volume is the product of the caller's widths | $10^{-14}$ relative | round-off of a three-factor product |
| `test_coordinate` | a degenerate $x_1$ beside live axes has width 5 | $10^{-14}$ absolute | round-off of one difference |

: Tests of the Cartesian metric. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-cartesian-tests}

The cases are `cell_volume_is_the_product_of_the_callers_widths` ([`test_coordinate.cpp:781-787`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_coordinate.cpp#L781-L787)) and
`a_degenerate_axis_beside_live_ones` ([`test_coordinate.cpp:789-806`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_coordinate.cpp#L789-L806)). Both run on CPU only, one block, one
rank. Their pass status at the pin was not run for this chapter (missing evidence).

### Limits

No known limits beyond those of the global grid (@sec-ch03-globalgrid). The divergence of a mesh-generator grid is not
tested at the pin (not measured). The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix of chapter 12.
